name: Music trivia (hard)
description: 50 hard questions about composers, instruments, genres, famous songs and musicians (no lyrics quoted). Written by Claude from cited web pages; every question names its page. Checked by a second model pass; the questions it flagged were corrected or left out.

source.name: Web pages cited on each question

items.question: Who conducted the 1913 Paris premiere of Stravinsky's The Rite of Spring?
items.explain: Diaghilev's Ballets Russes premiered the work at the Théâtre des Champs-Élysées on 29 May 1913 with Pierre Monteux conducting.

source.title: The Rite of Spring – Boston Symphony Orchestra

items.question: Which painter and designer is credited with the costumes and staging for the 1913 premiere of The Rite of Spring?
items.explain: The premiere had choreography by Vaslav Nijinsky and costumes and staging by Nicholas Roerich.

source.title: The riotous premiere of Stravinsky's Rite of Spring

items.question: What is the subtitle of Stravinsky's The Rite of Spring?
items.explain: The ballet's subtitle is "Pictures of Pagan Russia in Two Parts", reflecting its scenario of primitive spring rituals.

items.question: What term did Berlioz use for the recurring theme that runs through all five movements of his Symphonie fantastique?
items.explain: Berlioz called the recurring theme representing the artist's obsession with his beloved the idée fixe. Wagner's leitmotifs are a related later idea.

items.question: Berlioz's Symphonie fantastique grew from his infatuation with which actress, whom he first saw playing Ophelia in Hamlet?
items.explain: The story of the symphony came from Berlioz's despair and love for Harriet Smithson, who had dazzled him in a Paris production of Hamlet.

source.title: Hector Berlioz - Discussion on Symphonie Fantastique

items.question: What is the name of Berlioz's work for speaker and music that was conceived as a sequel to the Symphonie fantastique and reuses its idée fixe?
items.explain: Lélio, Op. 14b, mixes music with spoken text and is a sequel to the Symphonie fantastique. It begins and ends with the idée fixe.

items.question: The melody Berlioz used for the idée fixe was borrowed from his 1828 Prix de Rome entry that took second prize. What was that cantata?
items.explain: The idée fixe melody was lifted from Berlioz's 1828 cantata Herminie, which took second prize in his second attempt at the Prix de Rome.

items.question: In the finale of Berlioz's Symphonie fantastique, the idée fixe returns as a trivial, vulgar dance tune. Which instrument plays it?
items.explain: In the Witches' Sabbath finale the idée fixe is distorted into a dance tune played on the E-flat clarinet.

items.question: Which conductor commissioned Bartók's Concerto for Orchestra in 1943 through his foundation?
items.explain: The Koussevitzky Music Foundation commissioned the work in memory of Natalie Koussevitzky. Koussevitzky then led the Boston Symphony in the premiere.

source.title: Concerto for Orchestra – Boston Symphony Orchestra

items.question: Bartók's Concerto for Orchestra includes a satirical treatment of a march theme from which Shostakovich symphony?
items.explain: Bartók mocked the march theme from Shostakovich's Seventh ("Leningrad") Symphony, which he had heard on a radio broadcast.

source.title: Béla Bartók: Concerto for Orchestra – Sofia Philharmonic

items.question: Which Hungarian violinist and friend of Bartók helped spur Koussevitzky into commissioning the Concerto for Orchestra?
items.explain: Without Koussevitzky and Bartók's Hungarian friend Joseph Szigeti urging him on, Bartók might never have written the piece.

source.title: Concerto for Orchestra – Boston Symphony Orchestra

items.question: Why did Bartók call his 1943 work a concerto rather than a symphony?
answers: Each orchestral section is treated in a soloistic, virtuosic way
Each movement is built as a strict fugue on a folk theme
The orchestra only accompanies a single solo instrument
The structure follows a dance suite rather than sonata form
items.correct: Each orchestral section is treated in a soloistic, virtuosic way
items.explain: Bartók said that since each instrument group is treated soloistically and virtuosically, he chose "concerto" over "symphony".

source.title: Why Did Bartók Name This Work a "Concerto for Orchestra"?

items.question: In Charles Ives's The Unanswered Question, which solo instrument repeatedly poses the question-like theme?
items.explain: Strings play simple harmonies while a trumpet repeats a question-like theme that the flutes answer dissonantly.

items.question: In 1908 Ives paired The Unanswered Question with which piece under the title Two Contemplations?
items.explain: Ives originally presented The Unanswered Question together with Central Park in the Dark as Two Contemplations.

items.question: Which Harlem venue hosted the early-1940s jam sessions where Gillespie, Parker, Monk and Kenny Clarke helped shape bebop?
items.explain: From 1941 Gillespie, Parker, Monk and Clarke played together at Minton's Playhouse on 118th Street in Harlem.

items.question: Which guitarist is named alongside Gillespie, Monk, Clarke and Parker among the originators of bebop?
items.explain: Britannica lists guitarist Charlie Christian among the players from whom bebop originated in the early 1940s.

items.question: Dizzy Gillespie's January 1945 recording "Be-Bop" was at first known by what title?
items.explain: Gillespie wrote and recorded the 78 in January 1945, and it was first known as Dizzy's Fingers. Disc jockeys and writers then adopted "bebop" for the style.

items.question: From 1939 to 1941, Dizzy Gillespie was a principal soloist in the band of which bandleader?
items.explain: Gillespie was one of the principal soloists in Cab Calloway's band between 1939 and 1941.

source.title: Dizzy Gillespie: a founding father of the 'bebop' revolution

items.question: Which pianist played instead of Bill Evans on the blues-oriented "Freddie Freeloader" from Kind of Blue?
items.explain: Davis had Wynton Kelly play on "Freddie Freeloader", the album's most blues-oriented track, in place of Bill Evans.

items.question: The Miles Davis composition "So What" is set in which mode?
items.explain: "So What" is modal jazz built on 16 bars of D Dorian, eight of E♭ Dorian and eight more of D Dorian.

items.question: Bill Evans's liner notes describe "All Blues" as a twelve-measure blues form in which time signature?
items.explain: The liner notes call it a 6/8 twelve-measure blues form that gets its mood from a few modal changes.

items.question: Which drummer joined bassist Paul Chambers in the rhythm section on Kind of Blue?
items.explain: The Library of Congress essay notes that Paul Chambers and drummer Jimmy Cobb kept the music swinging on the album.

source.title: "Kind of Blue"--Miles Davis (1959) Added to the National Registry: 2002

items.question: Which of these was an early name for the theremin?
items.explain: The theremin was originally known as the ætherphone, etherphone, thereminophone or termenvox.

items.question: On a theremin, how does the player raise the pitch?
answers: Moving a hand away from the pitch antenna
Moving a hand closer to the volume antenna
Moving a hand closer to the pitch antenna
items.correct: Moving a hand closer to the pitch antenna
items.explain: Higher notes come from moving the hand closer to the pitch antenna. Louder notes come from moving the hand away from the volume antenna.

items.question: Which modern instrument is routinely used to play the parts J.S. Bach wrote for the oboe da caccia?
items.explain: The oboe da caccia is an alto oboe and a forerunner of the English horn, which is now sometimes used for Bach's parts for it.

items.question: Which Bach work is a famous example of combining two viole da braccio with two viole da gamba?
items.explain: Bach's Sixth Brandenburg Concerto (1721) pairs two viole da braccio with two viole da gamba.

items.question: Messiaen's Quartet for the End of Time is scored for violin, cello, piano and which wind instrument?
items.explain: The eight-movement quartet is for clarinet, violin, cello and piano, the instruments and players available in the prison camp.

source.title: Quartet for the End of Time

items.question: Which biblical text did Messiaen cite in his preface as the subject and inspiration of the Quartet for the End of Time?
items.explain: Messiaen cited verses from chapter 10 of the Revelation of John as the work's subject and direct inspiration.

source.title: Olivier Messiaen :: Quatuor pour la Fin du Temps

items.question: Messiaen's Quartet for the End of Time often uses rhythmic patterns based on which kind of numbers?
items.explain: Britannica notes his patterns are frequently based on prime numbers, especially 5, 7, 11 and 13.

source.title: Quartet for the End of Time

items.question: The 1936 Pravda editorial "Muddle Instead of Music" condemned which Shostakovich opera?
answers: Lady Macbeth of the Mtsensk District
items.correct: Lady Macbeth of the Mtsensk District
items.explain: Stalin saw Lady Macbeth in 1936, and the Pravda review condemned it. Shostakovich then withdrew his Fourth Symphony and wrote his Fifth.

source.title: A Soviet's Response to Just Criticism - Shostakovich Symphony No. 5

items.question: In what year was Shostakovich's Fourth Symphony, withdrawn before its planned premiere, first heard?
items.explain: Shostakovich shelved the Fourth Symphony in 1936 amid official criticism, and it was not heard until 1961.

source.title: Shostakovich's Fifth Symphony: The Unlikely Triumph of Freedom

items.question: Who wrote the libretto for Monteverdi's L'Orfeo?
items.explain: L'Orfeo (1607) is an opera by Claudio Monteverdi with a libretto by Alessandro Striggio.

items.question: The earliest surviving opera, Euridice, is the work of which composer?
items.explain: Jacopo Peri's Dafne is generally recognised as the first opera, and his Euridice is the earliest that survives. Monteverdi's L'Orfeo is the earliest still regularly performed.

items.question: In which city was Monteverdi's L'Orfeo first performed in 1607?
items.explain: L'Orfeo was written for a court performance during the annual Carnival at Mantua and first performed at the Ducal Palace there.

items.question: What does the title of the collection Il cimento dell'armonia e dell'inventione, which opens with Vivaldi's The Four Seasons, mean in English?
answers: The Struggle of Passion and Reason
The Contest between Harmony and Invention
The Dance of Heaven and Earth
The Trial of Melody and Rhythm
items.correct: The Contest between Harmony and Invention
items.explain: The Four Seasons are the first four concertos of Vivaldi's collection "The Contest between Harmony and Invention".

items.question: Around 1706, which ailment forced the newly ordained Vivaldi to give up saying Mass?
items.explain: Asthmatic attacks forced Vivaldi, a newly ordained priest, to stop reciting Mass around 1706.

source.title: Antonio Vivaldi: The Four Seasons and beyond

items.question: Leonard Bernstein's 1973 Norton Lectures at Harvard took their title from a piece by which composer?
items.explain: Ives's The Unanswered Question inspired Bernstein's Norton Lectures of the same title at Harvard in 1973.

items.question: Which instrument did Dizzy Gillespie play at about twelve, before taking up the trumpet at fourteen?
items.explain: Gillespie played the trombone at about twelve and took up the trumpet at fourteen.

source.title: Dizzy Gillespie: a founding father of the 'bebop' revolution

items.question: What was the name of the first label Berry Gordy formed in 1959, which later grew into Motown?
items.explain: Gordy formed Tamla Records in 1959 and bought the Detroit house that became Hitsville U.S.A.

items.question: When Motown moved its headquarters to Los Angeles in 1972, which Gordy family member refused to move and ran the remaining Detroit office?
items.explain: Esther Gordy Edwards refused to move to California and was put in charge of what remained of the Detroit office in the Hitsville building.

items.question: In 1988 Berry Gordy sold Motown to which company?
items.explain: Gordy sold Motown in 1988 to MCA and the investment firm Boston Ventures. Boston Ventures later sold it to PolyGram, in 1993.

items.question: In which Texas city did Robert Johnson make his first recordings in November 1936?
items.explain: Johnson's first session took place on 23, 26 and 27 November 1936 at the Gunter Hotel in San Antonio. His second round of recordings was made in Dallas in 1937.

items.question: Who produced Robert Johnson's 1936 and 1937 recording sessions?
items.explain: Both of Johnson's recording sessions, in San Antonio and Dallas, were produced by Don Law.

items.question: Robert Johnson's two recording sessions produced how many distinct songs?
items.explain: The two sessions produced 29 distinct songs, plus surviving alternate takes.

items.question: The title of Robert Johnson's "32-20 Blues" refers to what?
items.explain: The title refers to .32-20 Winchester ammunition, which could be used in handguns and smaller rifles.

items.question: Who played the prominent harpsichord part on the Beatles' "Fixing a Hole"?
items.explain: Producer George Martin played the harpsichord part because McCartney felt it important to perform the bass part himself.

items.question: For the first session of "Fixing a Hole", the Beatles used which London studio, their first British studio other than Abbey Road for an EMI recording?
items.explain: Abbey Road was unavailable on 9 February 1967, so the band recorded the first session at Regent Sound.

items.question: The crowd sounds heard at the start of the Beatles' "Sgt. Pepper's Lonely Hearts Club Band" were recorded by George Martin during a live recording of which stage show?
items.explain: The crowd sounds were recorded in the early 1960s by Martin during a live recording of the stage show Beyond the Fringe.

source.title: Sgt. Pepper's Lonely Hearts Club Band (song)

items.question: Which band, recording in a neighbouring studio, gained entry to a Beatles session for "Lovely Rita"?
items.explain: Pink Floyd were recording next door and got into the "Lovely Rita" session through their producer, Norman Smith, a former Beatles engineer.

items.question: Which Beatles road manager suggested that Sgt. Pepper act as compère and that the album have a reprise at the end?
items.explain: Road manager Neil Aspinall suggested both Sgt. Pepper as compère and the reprise at the album's end.

source.title: Sgt. Pepper's Lonely Hearts Club Band (song)
